$comment: Controls this repository defers BY NAME and deliberately does not give a lane in .github/workflows/**. gate-deferral-lane.sh reads this file: a deferred control that no workflow names is a failure UNLESS it is written down here with the reason, and every entry is printed by name on every run. The list is also checked backwards - an entry for a control that no longer exists, that nothing defers any more, or that has since acquired a real lane is itself a failure, because an exemption nobody can be caught by is how a hole becomes permanent.
$comment_not_a_tolerance: Nothing here is excused from measurement. Each entry says where the control DOES run. What it buys is that the absence of a CI lane is a written decision with an owner, rather than a silence that reads like coverage.

gate-governance-drift.sh.reason: It measures the LIVE repository through the GitHub API, and reading branch protection needs the `administration` scope, which the GITHUB_TOKEN a workflow receives cannot be granted - that permission does not exist for workflow tokens. Run in CI it would report 2 for ever, which run-all.sh names as the fastest route to somebody switching the suite off. Giving it a CI lane needs a fine-grained PAT with Administration:read, and that is the owner's decision.
gate-governance-drift.sh.runs: locally, against an authenticated gh: scripts/gates/run-all.sh with EHS_LIVE_REPO set
